古箏是中國傳統弦樂器，距今已有二千五百多年歷史，最早於秦朝出現故又稱「秦箏」。樂: The guzheng is a traditional Chinese string instrument with a history of more than 2,500 years; because it first appeared in the Qin dynasty it is also called the “Qin zheng”. The instrument is rectangular and consists of a wooden soundbox, silk strings and movable bridges. Its timbre is clear and transparent, with the warm gentleness of an Eastern character, and its range is wide, up to four octaves. It spread from China through East Asia, developing into the koto in Japan and the gayageum in Korea. It was traditionally used in court and literati yayue music, and today it is widely used in folk music performance, teaching and creative composition.
古箏面板多採用白松或杉木製作，具有良好共鳴效果。底板及側板通常選用楸木、梧桐木等: The soundboard of the guzheng is usually of white pine or fir, which resonates well. The back and sides are usually of catalpa, paulownia or similar woods. The bridges are movable and traditionally of rosewood. The strings were originally silk; today nylon or steel-wound strings are usual. The decorative parts at the head and tail are often rosewood or another hardwood. Some fine guzheng use precious woods such as sandalwood or huanghuali, which improves both the sound and the appearance.
古箏音色清亮透徹，兼具溫潤柔和的特質，具有獨特的東方韻味。其音域寬廣，跨度可達四: The guzheng's timbre is clear and transparent and at the same time warm and gentle, with a distinctive Eastern character. Its range is wide, spanning up to four octaves; the treble is crisp and bright, the middle register warm and full, and the bass deep and powerful. The guzheng amplifies the strings through the resonating cavity of the soundboard, which produces rich overtones and sustain and gives the timbre many layers. Beside the force and penetration of the piano, the guzheng is softer and more retiring; beside the guitar, its tone is clearer and more transparent, with a longer resonance. Its distinctive plucking techniques and its pressed-string vibrato produce a wide range of colour, from bright and leaping to deep and drawn out, with great expressive power.
吉他齊特琴屬弦鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs編號314.122，為詩特: The guitar zither is a chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 314.122, a kind of fretless zither. It was patented on 29 May 1894 by Friederich Menzenhauer, came into use at the end of the nineteenth century, and was later mass-produced in the United States and Germany, continued by the Oscar Schmidt company and other makers. In 1902 the Sears catalogue promoted the Deweylin harp as a kind of fretless zither, saying it combined the mandolin, the guitar and the zither. Unlike the autoharp it has no damper bars; unlike the concert zither it has no fingerboard; its name comes from its timbre.
